definition: Explicit resolved states for governed public slots where primary official evidence establishes that the requested observation is unavailable, or where a governed phase decision retires/replaces a weak placeholder. P22 time-sensitive closures may also resolve a snapshot when the exact current county observation is unavailable under explicit freshness, geography or measure-definition contracts. These states never manufacture a zero, proxy, regional inheritance or synthetic observation.

states.source: National Treasury Budget Review and Outlook Paper 2025, Table 10; source data Controller of Budget
states.reason: Narok is explicitly shown without a pending-bills amount in the final Table 10 county breakdown because the entity did not submit pending-bills data. The Atlas preserves this as official non-submission; it is not zero and is not reverse-engineered from the budget percentage column.

states.source: NACADA National Survey on the Status of Drugs and Substance Use in Kenya 2022
states.reason: The 2022 NACADA survey was designed to provide national, regional, urban and rural prevalence estimates. Although sampled clusters were spread across all 47 counties, the official report does not publish a statistically defensible county prevalence series. Regional estimates are therefore not inherited or allocated to counties, and county sampling uncertainty is not fabricated.

states.source: KNBS / Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development — National Agriculture Production Report 2024, Annex 1
states.reason: The original generic county-dominant-crop placeholder cannot provide one comparable 47-county measure because the crop and unit would vary by county. P19 already exposes fixed-definition maize area, maize production and transparent maize yield for all 47 counties from Annex 1 of the official National Agriculture Production Report 2024. P21 therefore retires and replaces the generic slot rather than duplicating evidence or mixing unlike crop measures.

states.period_label: KNEC examination transition reviewed through FY 2023/24 · P21 replacement decision
states.source: Kenya National Examinations Council — official examination transition and results publication model
states.reason: The original generic 'Mean KCPE / KCSE score' county placeholder is not a stable, comparable 47-county series. KNEC records 2023 as the final KCPE examination and the national transition to competency-based assessment, while official results are released at candidate/institution level and published examination statistics do not establish a single governed county mean that can be carried consistently across the changing assessment systems. P21 therefore retires the mixed exam-score placeholder rather than scraping unofficial county league tables or manufacturing aggregates. The Atlas retains source-backed county education evidence through school-attendance, public-school and teacher-establishment indicators, without presenting those measures as exam scores.

states.source: P21 governed county-licensing comparability review; replacement indicators sourced from KNBS Gross County Product 2025
states.reason: The original licensed-business count/year-on-year placeholder cannot support one defensible 47-county comparable series: county licensing publications and administrative systems have inconsistent coverage, vintages and licensing definitions, and the Atlas has no governed national source that standardises those counts across all counties. P21 therefore retires the profile-wide business-licence slot rather than stitching together opportunistic county values or treating non-publication as zero. The linked KNBS source supports the replacement economic indicators, not a business-licence count. The Atlas retains stronger 47/47 official county economic evidence through Gross County Product and fixed-definition agriculture/manufacturing GVA and GCP-share measures.

states.period_label: August–September 2023 Health Facility Census · P21 replacement decision
states.source: Ministry of Health — Kenya Health Facility Census Report September 2023
states.reason: The original 'Facilities with electricity/water (%)' placeholder combines two distinct amenity concepts into one undefined county percentage. The published 2023 Health Facility Census reports reliable-water and reliable-power availability as facility-readiness results, while its published county table covers census coverage rather than a governed 47-county combined water/power amenity series. P21 therefore retires the mixed placeholder instead of reverse-engineering county values from figures, combining unlike measures, or fabricating missing values. The Atlas retains source-backed county health-infrastructure evidence through facility stock and facility density; those successors measure supply, not electricity/water access.

states.source: Ministry of Health — Service Availability and Readiness Assessment (SARA) Main Report, Table 18
states.reason: The original county hospital-bed occupancy/utilisation placeholder cannot be filled defensibly from the published SARA report. The Ministry of Health reports a national average inpatient bed occupancy rate of 46%, but does not publish a governed 47-county occupancy table in the report. Table 18 does publish a complete 47-county percentage of facilities offering inpatient services, with facility denominators. P21 therefore retires the occupancy placeholder rather than allocating the national 46% to counties or treating service availability as utilisation. The new inpatient-service-availability indicator is a clearly labelled successor and must not be interpreted as bed occupancy.

states.source: KNBS and ICF — Kenya Demographic and Health Survey 2022, Volume 1, Table 2.21.3C
states.reason: The original Inua Jamii beneficiary placeholder is an administrative person-count concept, but no citable complete 47-county administrative beneficiary table has been identified. KDHS 2022 Table 2.21.3C instead publishes a complete 47-county household survey measure: percentage of households receiving a cash transfer or any social assistance. P21 retires the administrative placeholder rather than converting a household percentage into a person count, and promotes the KDHS measure as a separately named successor with survey denominators and ranking withheld.

states.source: KNBS — 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census, Volume IV, Table 2.36
states.reason: The original vehicle-registration placeholder is an administrative registered-vehicle stock/count concept, but no governed complete 47-county NTSA registration table has been identified. KNBS 2019 KPHC Volume IV Table 2.36 publishes complete 47-county percentages of conventional households owning motorcycles and cars. P21 therefore retires the registration-count placeholder rather than converting ownership percentages into vehicle counts or registration rates, and promotes the two census ownership measures as separately named successors. No synthetic combined vehicle-ownership percentage is created because household asset ownership can overlap.

states.period_label: 2025 provisional · Economic Survey 2026 · P21 replacement decision
states.source: KNBS Economic Survey 2026, Table 11.9; underlying source Kenya Rural Roads Authority
states.reason: The original 'Classified road length' county placeholder is broader and insufficiently defined for a single comparable county series. KNBS Economic Survey 2026 Table 11.9 publishes a complete 47-county fixed-definition 2025 series for Class C rural roads, sourced to the Kenya Rural Roads Authority and informed by the 2025 Road Inventory and Condition Surveys. P21 therefore retires the ambiguous generic slot and promotes Class C rural road length as a separately named successor. Class C is not presented as the entire county road network, and the Atlas preserves the table's published Total column rather than recomputing it from rounded paved/unpaved display components.

states.period_label: as of 1 Sep 2026 · latest county reference month Jun 2026 (stale)
states.source: National Drought Management Authority — County Drought Early Warning Bulletins
states.refresh_trigger: Replace this evidence state when an official NDMA county bulletin is available within the P22 freshness tolerance and its county alert state is deterministically extracted.
states.reason: The official NDMA county listing exposes June 2026 as the latest county bulletin reference month for the governed ASAL counties. At the 1 September 2026 P22 snapshot, June is three calendar months behind and fails the contract's maximum two-month current-label tolerance. The newer July 2026 national bulletin is control evidence only and cannot be inherited to counties. P22 therefore resolves the current county alert slot as officially unavailable under the freshness contract rather than displaying a stale warning as current.

states.period_label: as of 1 Sep 2026 · 2026 LRA listed, classification payload not deterministically resolved
states.source: National Drought Management Authority / Kenya Food Security Steering Group — Long Rains Assessment 2026
states.refresh_trigger: Replace this evidence state when the official 2026 LRA payload or equivalent official endpoint exposes source-supported whole-county phases and explicit validity intervals that pass the P22 geography/freshness gate.
states.reason: The official NDMA resource index confirms the Long Rains Assessment National Report 2026 was published in August 2026, but the governed pipeline does not yet have a stable official payload exposing exact classification geography, county phase values and current/projected validity intervals. The older 2025 Short Rains Assessment windows ended by June 2026. P22 therefore does not infer IPC phases from a listing, a report title, an expired classification, livelihood-zone evidence or partial-county evidence; the exact current whole-county classification is resolved as officially unavailable for this snapshot.

states.period_label: as of 1 Sep 2026 · KMD Aug 2026 products reviewed
states.source: Kenya Meteorological Department — August 2026 agrometeorological bulletin and official climate products
states.refresh_trigger: Replace this evidence state when KMD publishes a direct county anomaly table or an approved gridded KMD source can be deterministically aggregated to counties with baseline, window, method and boundary metadata preserved.
states.reason: Fresh official KMD material is available, including the August 2026 agrometeorological bulletin, but it provides qualitative county-group forecasts and station-level review rather than one direct numeric rainfall/temperature anomaly value for each governed county with an explicit climatological baseline and county aggregation method. Historical KMD anomaly maps are not reverse-engineered into county numbers. P22 therefore resolves the exact governed county anomaly observation as officially unavailable rather than manufacturing values from qualitative language, stations, map colours or unapproved spatial interpolation.

states.source: KNBS — 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census Reports
states.reason: KNBS's 2019 KPHC publication does not publish population as a direct current-290-constituency table. Published county/sub-county/administrative-unit values are not inherited or cross-walked without an authoritative boundary mapping; the older KNBS constituency table predates the current 2012-01 constituency configuration.
states.refresh_trigger: KNBS publishes a direct current-290 constituency population table or an authoritative 2019 administrative-unit to 2012-01 constituency crosswalk.

states.source: KNBS — 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census Reports
states.reason: KNBS's 2019 KPHC publication does not publish average household size as a direct current-290-constituency table. County/sub-county values are not inherited, and lower administrative-unit household counts are not aggregated without an authoritative constituency crosswalk; the older KNBS constituency table predates the current 2012-01 constituency configuration.
states.refresh_trigger: KNBS publishes a direct current-290 constituency household-size table or an authoritative 2019 administrative-unit to 2012-01 constituency crosswalk.

states.source: National Government Constituencies Development Fund Board — disbursement and audit/public-accountability pages
states.reason: The NG-CDF Board publishes constituency allocations and disbursements, and states that Fund utilisation is tracked through constituency internal audit and Board/Auditor-General oversight. The public national surface reviewed does not publish one comparable utilisation-rate percentage for all current 290 constituencies. Disbursement is explicitly a transfer of funds to constituencies for approved projects and is not treated as expenditure/utilisation. The Atlas therefore does not derive a utilisation percentage from allocation or disbursement amounts.
states.refresh_trigger: Replace this closure when the NG-CDF Board, Auditor-General or another primary official authority publishes a nationally comparable current-290 constituency utilisation/expenditure table with a common fiscal period and denominator.

states.source: Ministry of Health — Kenya Master Health Facility Registry (KMHFR)
states.reason: KMHFR provides official facility records with constituency location and can support constituency facility counts. The Atlas indicator, however, is health facilities assessed per 10,000 residents and requires a population denominator aligned to the current 290-constituency boundary and reference period. The governed P23 census review found no direct current-290 constituency population series or authoritative crosswalk supporting that denominator. A facility count is not relabelled as a population density, and no county/sub-county population is inherited downward.
states.refresh_trigger: Replace this closure when an authoritative current-290 constituency population denominator aligned to the facility-count reference period is published or can be deterministically derived under an approved boundary crosswalk.
